newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal rightist split hardens anti-EMU line.
newsitem.headline: Portugal rightist split hardens anti-EMU line.

text.p: A crisis in Portugal's rightwing Popular Party (PP) signals a hardening of its opposition to the European single currency, analysts said on Wednesday.

Manuel Monteiro quit as head of Portugal's third biggest party on Tuesday night as it was being torn apart by his rivalry with a "Eurosceptic" former newspaper editor, Paulo Portas, and called an extraordinary congress to elect his successor.

Monteiro challenged Portas to stand for the party leadership at the congress which he said should take place after October 13 when regional elections on Portugal's semi-autonomous islands of Madeira and the Azores are due to take place.
"Portas is a more radical 'Eurosceptic' than Monteiro," said a Western diplomat. "He is a very charismatic figure who is very effective at getting his message across."
Portas was believed to hold strong views against the planned European single currency which he considered to be a threat to Portugal's national sovereignty, analysts said.
The PP wants to hold a referendum on revision of the Maastricht treaty, criticises the border-free Schengen agreement and says it would tighten regulations on agricultural imports.
But the PP, with just 15 seats in the 230-seat parliament, was unlikely to alter the overall course of Portuguese government policy, which strongly favoured European integration, analysts said.
Socialist Prime Minister Antonio Guterres says he is determined that Portugal should join the first group of nations to take part in the single currency before the end of the century.
